references.text: The children of Israel did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, which is a similar example of incomplete conquest of the land.
The children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of several cities, showing the same pattern of incomplete conquest.
Judges tells of several tribes that did not drive out the original inhabitants, confirming the pattern mentioned in Joshua.
Geshur is mentioned as one of the peoples who remained in the land, consistent with them not being driven out.
David's wife Maacah was the daughter of the king of Geshur, showing that Geshur continued as an independent kingdom.
Geshur and Maacath are mentioned as border regions for the lands given to the two and a half tribes east of the Jordan.
